package_info.why_malicious: The analyzed packages and payloads are associated with credential theft, ransomware, banking trojans, adware distribution, anti-forensics, and covert command-and-control (C&C) operations. They exhibit behaviors such as process injection, file encryption, abuse of accessibility services, browser extension hijacking, evidence destruction, and steganographic payload delivery, all of which are indicative of advanced, multi-stage malware campaigns targeting financial data, user credentials, and system integrity.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Kronos banking Trojan code (not shown in report, but referenced as credential stealing and banking malware)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects itself into browser processes, intercepts user credentials entered into banking websites, and exfiltrates them to a remote command-and-control server, enabling credential theft and financial fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting user credentials from browser processes and exfiltrating them to external servers is a hallmark of banking malware and is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not inject into browser processes or capture and transmit user credentials without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may simulate process injection and credential interception in controlled, authorized environments for security assessment purposes.
key_indicators: process injection into browser memory space
network exfiltration to external C2 infrastructure

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Cerber ransomware code (not shown in report, but referenced as ransomware with credential and cryptocurrency theft features)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and encrypts user files, harvests private credentials from web browsers, attempts to locate and steal cryptocurrency wallet information, and transmits this data to a remote server, resulting in data loss, ransom demand, and financial theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypting user files for ransom, stealing browser credentials, and targeting cryptocurrency wallets are all highly malicious actions associated with ransomware and financial malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not encrypt user files without user-initiated backup or protection workflows, nor should it access or exfiltrate sensitive credentials or wallet data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup software may access and copy files, but does not encrypt for ransom or exfiltrate credentials and wallet information.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Svpeng Android banking Trojan code (not shown in report, but referenced as keylogger using Accessibility Services)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses Android Accessibility Services to log keystrokes and capture sensitive information entered by the user, then transmits the captured data to a remote server, enabling credential theft and unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing Accessibility Services to capture keystrokes and exfiltrate sensitive data is a well-known tactic of Android banking malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not use Accessibility Services for keylogging or data exfiltration; such use is a clear violation of user privacy and platform policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility features are intended to assist users with disabilities, not to capture or transmit sensitive input data.
key_indicators: Accessibility Services abuse for input capture

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious Chrome extension code (not shown in report, but referenced as distributing adware and potentially hijacking user sessions)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects unauthorized advertisements into web pages, may hijack user sessions or redirect browser traffic, and can potentially capture user credentials, resulting in adware distribution and risk of credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hijacking browser extensions to inject ads, redirect traffic, or steal credentials is a common attack vector for adware and credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions should not inject unauthorized ads, hijack sessions, or capture user credentials without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Ad blockers or productivity tools may modify web pages, but do so transparently and without malicious intent or data theft.
key_indicators: unauthorized ad injection via content scripts
network requests to ad or C2 domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dumbo tool code (not shown in report, but referenced as suspending webcam processes and deleting/manipulating video recordings)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and suspends processes associated with webcams, deletes or manipulates video recording files, and disables video capture, enabling anti-forensics and destruction of surveillance evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling surveillance devices and deleting or manipulating video evidence is a clear sign of anti-forensic activity, often used to conceal unauthorized actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not tamper with surveillance systems or destroy evidence files without explicit, authorized user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security or privacy tools may disable cameras for user privacy, but do not delete or manipulate surveillance recordings for anti-forensic purposes.
key_indicators: enumeration and suspension of webcam processes
deletion or manipulation of video files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steganography code (not shown in report, but referenced as hiding data in images for C&C or payload delivery)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code embeds malicious payloads or C&C instructions within image files using steganographic techniques, then extracts and executes the hidden data, enabling covert communication and stealthy payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hiding executable code or C&C data within image files is a sophisticated evasion technique used to bypass traditional security controls and enable covert operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal image files should not contain hidden executable code or C&C instructions; such manipulation is outside the scope of legitimate digital watermarking or image processing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Digital watermarking may embed non-executable metadata in images, but not malicious payloads or C&C data.
key_indicators: image file manipulation for data embedding
extraction and execution of payloads from images
covert C&C communication via image files

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via phishing, exploit kit, or malicious download.
Malware executes and performs credential theft, keylogging, or ad injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data or financial theft.

attack_chain.action: Malware encrypts files or manipulates system for ransom or anti-forensics.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data loss, ransom demand, or evidence destruction.

attack_chain.action: Malware communicates with C&C using covert channels (e.g., steganography).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sustained control or further payload delivery.

behavioral_signatures: Process injection into browser memory space
Abuse of Android Accessibility Services for keystroke logging
Unauthorized modification of browser extension code and ad injection
File system enumeration and encryption with ransom note creation
Enumeration and suspension of webcam processes with video file deletion
Embedding and extraction of data from image files using steganography
file_indicators: Unexpected modification of browser process memory
Unusual access to browser credential stores (e.g., Chrome Login Data, Firefox key4.db)
Chrome extension updates or code changes from untrusted sources
Creation of ransom notes (e.g., README.txt) or files with encrypted extensions (e.g., .cerber)
Deletion or manipulation of video surveillance files (e.g., .mp4, .avi) in known camera directories
Image files with appended or hidden payloads (e.g., abnormal file size, steganographic markers)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure (domains/IPs referenced in report, if any)
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credentials or cryptocurrency wallet data
Covert C&C via image file uploads/downloads to suspicious endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for process injection into browser memory, unauthorized access to credential stores, and abuse of Accessibility Services. Track Chrome extension updates and code modifications from untrusted sources. Detect file system enumeration, encryption activity, and ransom note creation. Alert on enumeration and suspension of webcam processes and deletion of video files. Analyze image files for steganographic payloads or C&C data. Correlate these behaviors with outbound network connections to suspicious domains or C2 infrastructure for comprehensive detection.
